Important new evidence•Peer-reviewed randomized trials•March 19, 2026

EVOKE trials find no clinical benefit from oral semaglutide in early AD

Two phase 3 trials did not show slower clinical progression despite biomarker changes.

Key quantitative results: At week 104, CDR-SB differences were −0.08 (95% CI −0.35 to 0.20; p=0.57) in evoke and 0.10 (−0.17 to 0.38; p=0.46) in evoke+, in the reported hybrid-HTC analysis.

Clinical TrialsManagementCSFp-tau217p-tau181Disease-modifying treatment

Added September 7, 2026 · DOI:10.1016/S0140-6736(26)00459-9; NCT04777396; NCT04777409

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

This tests treating established early AD; it does not answer every prevention question about GLP-1 drugs.

Study design

Double-blind trials randomized 1,855 and 1,953 amyloid-positive adults aged 55–85 with MCI or mild dementia to oral semaglutide or placebo.

Key quantitative results

  • At week 104, CDR-SB differences were −0.08 (95% CI −0.35 to 0.20; p=0.57) in evoke and 0.10 (−0.17 to 0.38; p=0.46) in evoke+, in the reported hybrid-HTC analysis.
  • Adverse-event treatment discontinuation was 17.1% (159/928) versus 8.2% (76/927), and 16.6% (162/976) versus 8.6% (84/977), respectively.

What changed

Definitive trial publication replaces inference from observational associations.

Strength of evidence

Large randomized evidence with negative clinical endpoints.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Does not support semaglutide as an AD treatment.

Field medical relevance

Use patient outcomes when interpreting target engagement.

Quanterix or platform relevance

Biomarker movement is not validated clinical utility.

Access or reimbursement relevance

No AD coverage determination follows from these trials.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Did biomarker changes establish benefit?
No; the clinical endpoints did not improve.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Sponsor funded; on-treatment estimand and discontinuation affect interpretation.
  • Primary-publication metadata and sponsor publication tables were verified; journal full text could not be retrieved.

Primary source · DOI · Sponsor publication tables, slides 7 and 11
